description: The peninsula (modern Turkey) that hosted much of Paul's missionary work and many of the churches addressed in the New Testament epistles — Ephesus, Colossae, Laodicea, Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe among them. Paul's team was at one point supernaturally redirected away from the province of Asia and toward Macedonia instead (Acts 16:6-10), and Peter's first letter is addressed to believers scattered across several of the region's provinces (1 Peter 1:1).
family_friendly_summary: Asia Minor is the large piece of land, today called Turkey, where Paul did much of his missionary work. Many churches from the New Testament were there, including Ephesus and Colossae. Once, God's Spirit stopped Paul from preaching in one part of it and sent him across the sea to Europe instead.
